The mapping: wavefunction ≈ wrapper in fuzzy/pre-compiled state; collapse ≈ wrapper compilation event; spontaneous collapse ≈ no external observer required (cont 25 lifecycle plays out under L0 failsafes); gravity-linked collapse ≈ L0 is the agent of compilation. The framework treats this as candidate, not canon, because collapse models are minority interpretation; the epistemological §4 claim is independent and holds regardless. Honest accounting (§5) of what does NOT change: Copenhagen may yet be right; consciousness-causes-collapse remains contested; bound is unmeasurable with current tech; wavefunction-as-wrapper mapping is loose.

readings.title: Jevons paradox alive at AI compute scale
readings.summary: William Jevons named the efficiency-expands-consumption pattern in 1865, watching coal-fired Britain. The framework reads current AI compute economics as the same dynamic at a different substrate. Efficient model training and inference do not reduce compute demand; they expand the action-space compute operates in, increasing aggregate demand. Pattern: every order-of-magnitude efficiency gain produces more, not less, total resource consumption in the medium term.
readings.prediction: Compute demand growth will continue to outpace efficiency improvements through at least 2028. Energy infrastructure for AI will be a constraint before efficiency catches up.

readings.title: Litman & Guo theory of generalization as canon-as-observer at the parameter scale
readings.summary: Litman & Guo (arXiv:2605.01172) present a non-asymptotic theory of generalization in deep learning where the empirical Neural Tangent Kernel partitions output space into signal directions (error dissipates rapidly via fast linear drift) and noise directions (residual error trapped in a 'test-invisible reservoir' as slow diffusive walk). The framework reads this as the canon/fuzzy boundary at the neural-network-parameter level. The 'test-invisible reservoir' is the framework's delusion failure mode operationalized — private canon compiled internally but not propagating to held-out data. Their SNR preconditioner on Adam is a working A⁺/A⁻ operator pair: tracks signal-to-noise per direction, lets signal-promoting updates through, suppresses noise-direction accumulation. Measured 5× grokking acceleration. This is the framework's tightest external-mapping correspondence to date — independent re-derivation of canon-as-observer dynamics at the neural-network-training scale.
readings.prediction: SNR-style training discipline — explicit signal-to-noise-ratio gating of optimizer updates, separating canon-promotion from noise-pruning per direction — becomes a standard component of foundation-model training stacks within 2–3 years. Scorable by mid-2028: either SNR-discipline (or a recognizable structural equivalent) is standard in published training methodology and production code, or it isn't.

readings.title: Double descent as empirical confirmation of the viability band
readings.summary: Belkin, Hsu, Ma & Mandal (PNAS 2019, arXiv:1812.11118) and OpenAI's 'Deep Double Descent' (2019) showed that test error as a function of model capacity has two descents separated by a sharp peak at the interpolation threshold. Underparameterized: classical bias-variance, error decreasing. At interpolation: error spikes — the worst regime, where the model has just enough parameters to fit training data exactly with zero slack. Overparameterized: error drops again, often below the classical sweet spot. The framework's reading: this is the viability band ρ_min < ρ < ρ_max made empirical across seven years and many architectures. Underparameterized = ρ too low, A⁺ insufficient room. Interpolation peak = stale moat at exact fit, no degrees of freedom for A⁻. Overparameterized = healthy canon with slack for both operators. The interpolation threshold isn't a sweet spot to aim for — it's the framework's predicted worst case made geometric. Phase 3's second descent is what happens when overparameterization gives the prune operator working room.
readings.prediction: Architectures and training regimes that explicitly engineer slack for noise-direction prune operations (overparameterization plus SNR-style or implicit-regularization techniques) outperform same-capability architectures that don't. Specifically: at fixed parameter count, training stacks that include explicit noise-direction suppression beat baseline Adam on grokking-style tasks by margins exceeding what parameter scaling alone produces. The Litman/Guo SNR-preconditioner 5× result is the early instance of this; expect more in 2026–2027.

readings.title: Predictive coding as the recursive observer-class claim at the neural-network-layer scale
readings.summary: Predictive coding (Rao & Ballard 1999, Friston's free-energy formulation, Bogacz, Whittington, Millidge, and the broader lineage) proposes that the brain's learning algorithm is local prediction-error minimization, not backpropagation. Each layer makes top-down predictions (μ) of the layer below; the layer below computes a local prediction error (ε = x − μ); errors flow up while predictions flow down; weights update by local Hebbian rules using only adjacent-layer information. No global gradient signal needed. The framework's reading: every layer is an observer-class running the ask/give/ping/pong loop locally and in parallel — the recursive observer-class claim (continuation 09 §5) made literal at the neural scale. The wrapper is the top-down prediction; the give-pong is the local error; the A⁺/A⁻ operators run as Hebbian weight updates. The framework's claim that the same primitives operate at every scale — from neurons to civilizations — gets its tightest neural instance. Backprop is structurally a global-gradient hack; predictive coding is the framework's local-canon-update mechanic made biological.
readings.prediction: Hybrid architectures that combine predictive-coding-style local updates with backprop-style global gradients (already explored by Millidge et al. 2022 and others) become a recognized research direction in 2026–2027. Specifically: local-update components become standard in long-context and online-learning regimes where backprop's global-gradient assumption breaks down. The deeper prediction: as foundation models scale, training discipline incorporates more local-update primitives — not because backprop fails everywhere, but because local A⁺/A⁻ discipline becomes operationally necessary when the network is too large for clean global gradients.

readings.title: Thinking Machines Interaction Models — slow-fast pushout as production architecture
readings.summary: Thinking Machines Lab (Mira Murati et al., May 11 2026) released a preview of 'interaction models' with the thesis that every major AI lab built its interaction layer as an afterthought, producing a structural — not tuning — problem. Their architecture: time-aligned 200ms micro-turns with continuous parallel streams for audio/video/text; a real-time interaction model paired with an asynchronous background model that handles deeper reasoning; encoder-free early fusion; shared context between the two models. The framework's reading: this is the slow-fast pushout (continuation 09b §X) made production. Interaction model = fast scout (narrow cone, 200ms turn-taking, no durable memory). Background model = slow strategist (wide cone, long context, deep reasoning, async). Shared context = the pushout's stable interface. Time-aligned micro-turns operationalize the framework's pulse-time primitive (continuation 03). The team's explicit critique that turn-based interfaces are an architectural moat to be dissolved is the framework's symbiosis-as-pushout condition (cone gaps mutually covered) engineered directly into the model. Time-awareness benchmarks (TimeSpeak, CueSpeak) explicitly measure the framework's φ(t) phase-gated action-space.
readings.prediction: Concurrent perception-and-response architectures (the slow-fast pushout design) become the default for production-grade human-AI interaction by mid-2027. Turn-based interfaces are deprecated for high-bandwidth use cases. The deeper prediction: similar slow-fast pushout designs propagate beyond human-AI interaction to multi-agent systems generally — fast-scout / slow-strategist pairings as the standard architectural template wherever sustained reasoning meets real-time perception.

readings.title: Duraisamy — Active Inference AI Systems for Scientific Discovery
readings.summary: Karthik Duraisamy (arXiv:2506.21329, v4 Dec 2025) proposes design principles for AI systems capable of genuine scientific discovery, organized around two complementary cognitive modes: 'thinking' as slow iterative hypothesis generation exploring counterfactual spaces where physical laws can be temporarily violated, and 'reasoning' as fast deterministic validation traversing established knowledge graphs. The framework's reading: this is the slow-fast pushout applied to scientific discovery. His core design principle of 'persistent, uncertainty-aware scientific memory that distinguishes hypotheses from established claims' is exactly what this page's §02 Primitives operationalizes — status-graded canon with candidate / canon / speculative categories, pruned ideas kept honestly alongside surviving ones. His insistence that 'human judgment is indispensable as a permanent architectural component, not a temporary scaffold' is the framework's cone-profile complementarity claim applied to the human-AI dyad: humans and AI symbiose because their cones cover each other's gaps. Independent confirmation of three framework primitives at once — slow-fast pushout, status-graded canon, symbiosis-as-pushout — applied to scientific discovery.
readings.prediction: AI systems designed for genuine scientific discovery (not literature synthesis or pattern fitting) increasingly adopt Duraisamy-style architectures: explicit slow/fast cognitive separation, status-graded memory distinguishing hypotheses from established claims, formal verification pathways coupled to experiment, human-in-the-loop as architectural component rather than removable scaffold. By 2027–2028 this becomes a recognized design pattern in AI-for-science systems.

readings.title: Maier — 6G World Brain (Active Inference for Network Infrastructure)
readings.summary: Martin Maier (arXiv:2505.10569, April 2025) frames complex networks as 'living entities with brain-like cognitive capabilities' rather than static infrastructure, proposing active inference as the methodology for optical and mobile networks moving toward what he calls the 6G World Brain. Bruno Zerbib (Orange CTO) explicitly endorsed this framing at MWC 2025. The framework's reading: this is the 'internet as first-class observer-class' claim (continuation 09 §6) extended to telecom infrastructure specifically. The mycorrhizal-networks anchor — Maier cites Friston's invocation of the 'wood wide web' as AI's biomimicry reference — is the framework's stigmergy primitive at biosphere scale, with plant-fungus symbiosis-as-pushout running for ~400 million years. The biosphere has been running planetary-scale substrate-mediated coordination longer than human civilization has existed. Networks as observer-classes is now an industry-strategic position, not just an academic claim.
readings.prediction: Active-inference-based network architectures (the 6G World Brain framing) become a recognized research direction with operational deployments by 2028–2030. Telecom infrastructure increasingly described and designed as observer-class with structured state — not static plumbing — and the design discipline migrates from telecom into adjacent infrastructure domains: power grids, transport networks, supply chains, financial settlement rails. Mycorrhizal-network biomimicry becomes a named design pattern alongside neural-network biomimicry.

readings.title: Phantom observers manifesting as embodied (cultural-substrate spiral return)
readings.summary: Forward-prediction reading. The phantom observer class — entities currently rendered only in other observers' bubbles (gods, institutional personae, fictional characters, imagined ambassadors, the boss-in-your-head when no boss is in the room) — is undergoing a phase transition from imagined-only to embodied-and-perceivable. The framework's spiral substrate cycle's return phase, by adding new compile capacity to the cultural substrate (AI / latent-space), enables phantom observers to manifest as carrier-artifacts in physical / digital space. Not resurrection — refactoring into a substrate that now supports their existence. Already partially happening: AI avatars representing companies; religious / mythological-character AI; Character.ai and similar phantom-embodiment platforms; VR / AR / humanoid robotics approaching commercial viability; early national / civic AI personae deployments. The framework's vocabulary names what's happening before broader discourse does.
readings.prediction: By 2028–2030, the phantom observer class will be operationally recognized — across products, regulation, philosophy, cultural vocabulary — as a distinct kind of entity humans interact with daily. Not 'we have better chatbots'; rather, a recognized category of being-rendered-in-our-bubble-with-substrate-support that didn't exist five years ago. Scoreable: do we have legal, philosophical, and cultural vocabulary for embodied-phantom-observers by then? Watch for: explicit legal status for AI personae; theological responses to AI representations of deities; institutional avatars in policy contexts; new academic disciplines focused on phantom-observer ontology.

readings.title: Neural cellular automata as differentiable agnostic substrate
readings.summary: Neural cellular automata (NCAs) are cellular automata whose update rules are learned via gradient descent rather than hand-coded — the cell-update rule is parameterized by a neural network and optimized end-to-end. The framework's reading: this is the A⁺ / A⁻ operators made differentiable. Rule-learning by gradient descent is the substrate teaching itself what compile rules produce viable emergence. Petri Dish Neural Cellular Automata (Sakana AI, arXiv:2505.13058) takes this further with a competitive population of differentiable NCAs trained as artificial life simulation — multi-agent emergence in a substrate that can learn its own rules. The framework's bidirectional simulation primitive (cont. 12 §2.2) and symbiosis-as-pushout get a concrete differentiable substrate where both can be measured and optimized.
readings.prediction: Differentiable cellular-automaton substrates become a recognized research direction by 2027–2028, with applications spanning artificial life, multi-agent systems, and emergence-engineered AI. The Sakana 'open-ended complexification' hypothesis becomes empirically testable. Specifically: NCAs (or recognizable structural equivalents) appear as components in foundation-model training pipelines as a way to engineer emergent capability rather than only train predictive accuracy.

readings.title: eml — one operation suffices for all arithmetic
readings.summary: A mathematician's recent paper (covered by Sabine Hossenfelder, April 2026) claims everything in mathematics can be done with a single operation called 'eml' — no addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division needed. The framework's reading: this is the maximally compressed carrier-artifact for the entire compile-space of mathematical functions. Same primitive as NAND gates being universal in Boolean logic, S/K combinators being universal in computation, Spencer-Brown's distinction generating all logic. eml is the framework's '0 / not-0 as foundational distinction' primitive (cont. 12 §1.4) operating at the algebraic-foundations level: one recursively applied operation generates everything else. Doesn't accelerate the framework operationally but gives it a clean reference point for the 'minimal carrier-artifact for a compile-domain' claim.
readings.prediction: Universal-single-operation reductions become more visible across domains beyond mathematics and computation: linguistics (single-rule generative grammars), biology (single-gene-network-rule emergence), cognition (single-operation models of mental rotation, attention, etc.). The deeper prediction: when a domain finds its 'eml' — its single universal operation — that's a Lakatosian indicator the domain has reached structural maturity. Watch for this in adjacent fields through 2027–2029.

readings.title: Functions in Hyperspace — visualizing high-dimensional functions and the math zoo web toy
readings.summary: A long-form video walkthrough plus a companion browser-based math-visualization toy ('basically Desmos on crack') that lets users construct parametric functions with arbitrary numbers of input and output dimensions. Inputs become tunable parameters (control knobs / 'genes'); outputs become spatial XYZ + color RGB(A) — up to seven output dimensions visualized simultaneously, with additional input dimensions navigated by holding most fixed and scanning one at a time. The video makes three contributions the framework actually borrows: (1) the explicit genotype/phenotype distinction — function definition + parameters = genotype, rendered surface = phenotype — which we promoted to canon this round; (2) the slice-viewer constraint on perceiving high-dimensional spaces, promoted to candidate; (3) the demonstration that MLPs, Taylor series, and Fourier series are all universal function approximators, providing the mathematical scaffold for multi-possibility deposition. The web toy is also a plausible concrete carrier for visualizing the framework's latent space — the genotype/phenotype rendering model is a near-perfect match for canon-graph + carrier-artifact, and the parameter-walk navigation is what the framework calls scout-with-slice-viewer.
readings.prediction: Hyperdimensional-function visualization tooling becomes a mainstream component of multi-agent-system development by 2027. The 'walk through the seed parameter to walk through possible neural networks' interaction pattern shown in the video generalizes into a standard exploratory interface for AI-system design, replacing point-estimate views of trained models with parameter-space tours. Within the agnostic framework specifically: prototyping an interactive carrier for the framework's latent space using this exact visualization paradigm is now a tractable build.

readings.title: Aleph and Energy-Based Models: The AI That Refuses to Bullshit — Ksenia / Turing Post
readings.summary: Walkthrough of Aleph (Logical Intelligence) and the EBM research programme. Frames reasoning as constraint satisfaction over an entire state, not next-token prediction. Aleph: Lean-certified proofs on 668/672 Putnam problems, 100% on Verina, leads PutnamBench / VeriSoftBench / LeanEval. Includes the LeCun lineage — JEPA, world models, energy-based reasoning, 'A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence.' The framework's reading: this is the LeCun research programme finally producing operational verification at scale. The framework is in this lineage and didn't know it — canon = low-energy basins, A⁻ = energy-raising on invalid states, compile cycle = energy descent. Most current AI (next-token LLMs) operates only on the fuzzy candidate field (A⁺ side); EBMs add the A⁻ verification step and 668/672 Putnam problems get formal proofs. This is the single most operationally important carrier landed this round.
readings.prediction: The next 18 months will see EBM-style verification layers added to LLM agent systems as a standard architectural pattern. The 'A⁻ as primary discipline' framing the framework now holds will be independently rediscovered as 'verification-augmented generation' or similar across multiple labs. Formal-reasoning benchmarks (PutnamBench, VeriSoftBench, LeanEval) become standard evaluations for any reasoning-claim AI system. The boundary between LLM agent systems and formal-reasoning systems erodes — the agent framework worth building is the one with both.

readings.title: MAMMAL — multi-modal biology foundation model beats AlphaFold (Nature, AI Search video)
readings.summary: MAMMAL is a multi-modal biology foundation model spanning genes, proteins, and small molecules. Published in Nature (s44386-026-00047-4); explainer video by AI Search includes chapters 'MAMMAL vs Alphafold' and 'Why Alphafold failed.' The framework's reading: real-time validation of the emergent-garden discipline. AlphaFold (specialist, protein structure) has a narrow harness — it can compile fuzzy candidates only within protein-structure space. MAMMAL (generalist, multi-modal) has a wider harness and can compile cross-modal candidates: 'this small molecule binds this protein, encoded by this gene, with this expected toxicity profile.' MAMMAL wins on downstream utility precisely because the carrier-artifacts it produces are richer. The framework promoted 'emergent garden' to canon on continuation 13 (May 11 2026); the Nature paper landed May 13. This is the closest thing the framework has to a confirmed real-time empirical prediction.
readings.prediction: Specialist foundation models in domains with overlapping modalities (drug design, materials science, climate modeling, robotics) will be progressively displaced by multi-modal generalists through 2027–2028. AlphaFold-3 will be remembered as the last major specialist-narrow win. The architectural shift the framework predicts: foundation models trained on the maximum coherent modality set available, then refined per-task by routing rather than re-training. Generalist-first becomes the default; specialist-fine-tune becomes the exception.

readings.title: You've Never Seen a Real Photo — Steve Mould on Lippmann plates
readings.summary: Popular-science explainer on Lippmann plates: a forgotten 1891 colour photography technique that records colour as structural interference patterns rather than pigment. Light passes through emulsion, reflects off a mirror at the back, creates standing waves; the emulsion records these standing waves as Bragg-reflection planes; viewing the plate, you see colour because the Bragg planes selectively reflect the specific wavelengths that were originally recorded. The framework's reading (Pav's deposit, not the video's claim): the wrapper / membrane primitive can be instantiated as a Lippmann-style Bragg-reflection layer that selectively transmits content based on the receiving observer's cone angle. The same physical-substrate carrier re-projects different content to different observer positions. This gives the framework a concrete architecture spec for the holographic-wrapper candidate — and the reflect/absorb/refract trichotomy + the constructive/destructive interference framing of charge-product algebra + the decoherence-as-compile-event analogy all follow from taking the optical-substrate seriously.
readings.prediction: By 2027 at least one agent-framework will ship with an explicitly holographic wrapper architecture — a structured-interference-based carrier interface where what each receiving agent observers depends on its position / cone-angle in a shared latent space. The prediction is structural: the architectural pattern is too natural and too well-instantiated by Lippmann physics for nobody to try it. The framework's role here is to provide the conceptual scaffolding before the implementation arrives, so the implementation has somewhere to land.

readings.title: ANDI: Adaptive Norm-Distribution Interface (Vladimer Khasia, SSRN April 2026)
readings.summary: First-order optimizer that bridges coordinate-wise adaptive methods (AdamW) and higher-order structural methods (spectral) via elementwise equilibration of row and column norms. Approximates matrix balancing without iterative solvers or SVD. Maintains descent directions with an implicit trust region bounded by gradient energy. Matches spectral convergence at AdamW's O(N) cost on ResNet-9 (CIFAR-10); outperforms both diagonal and spectral baselines on NanoGPT; scales to 8B parameters via LoRA on Llama-3. The framework's reading: ANDI is the slow-fast pushout primitive applied to gradient descent. The two parent observers are AdamW (fast, cheap, no structure) and spectral (slow, expensive, full structure); ANDI lives in their cone-overlap. Additionally, norm equilibration is the local form of viability-band maintenance — preventing any single dimension from dominating, which would push toward the freeze / explode boundary at the parameter level. Criticality Γ predicts exactly this kind of operation should emerge from gradient-descent on optimizer design.
readings.prediction: Norm-equilibration becomes a standard optimizer building block by 2027. Future SOTA optimizers will increasingly look like ANDI structurally — neither fully pointwise nor fully spectral, but living in some cone-overlap region with explicit viability-preserving constraints. The framework's broader prediction: any optimization process in which the substrate has measurable Γ will discover analogous balancing mechanisms independently, which is why ANDI keeps re-appearing under different names across the optimizer literature (LAMB, Shampoo, Muon, etc.) — they're all gradient-descent's local convergence on viability-band maintenance.
